solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parents wear identification

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, so two parents can be pas
to sport an item is to wear it showily

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad put on their identity badges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parents wear' reads as a plural subject and verb, but each word gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is carried abroad chiefly to prove who the holder is.

clue.text: Quite dry, sheltering in quarry

indicators.note: the dry piece takes cover inside the quarry piece

parts.note: a hunted animal is the hunter's prey
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol: dry

explanation.surface: Fairly arid weather, taking cover in a stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' suggests a stone pit; it is the hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, 'pretty good' means fairly or rather good, the same sense as quite.

clue.text: Attempts to get evidence overthrown in courts

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: someone who pries to find proof snoops

explanation.surface: Bids to have proof thrown out in the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' looks legal but is the verb of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned slang: a couple who canoodle are said to spoon, which is to woo or court.

clue.text: Is critical about one and is hurtful

indicators.note: the critic's word goes around the numeral piece

parts.note: a critic who slates something pans it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A critic's savage review that wounds its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hurts or distresses a person is said to give them pain: 'it grieves me' sense.

clue.text: Quickly try to get to end of precis

definitions.text: Quickly try to get to end of
definitions.meaning: to ... a fugitive or a fact is to chase it fast until it is found
a short summary of the main points

explanation.surface: A hurried attempt to reach the last line of a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the two-word verb phrase; the second is the noun, usually hyphenated.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick account of the main points, as in 'give me the latest', is a brief summary.

clue.text: Fires consuming hotel and sheds

indicators.note: the dismissal word eats up the letter for hotel

parts.note: an employer who fires staff sacks them
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Blazes engulf a hotel and its outbuildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fires' looks like flames; it means dismisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough huts and outhouses are crude wooden sheds.

clue.text: For just an instant, sound of organ

definitions.meaning: in a moment, so the word stands for a tiny interval
the thump made by the pumping heart

explanation.surface: A single brief note sounded on a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument; it is the body's pump.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulse of the heart is both very short and an audible thump.

clue.text: Handbag in two parts? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: split as hand and bag: a hand's slap or applause, then a catch or snare

explanation.surface: A shopper dismisses a two-piece handbag as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand gives the applause word and bag (to catch) gives the snare word, so the answer read in two halves is a jokey hand-bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, insincere talk meant to win applause is rubbish: drivel.

clue.text: No good players left, having been pipped

definitions.meaning: in a tennis draw the top-ranked players are seeds; when all are out the event is without them
pips are fruit stones, so pipped fruit has had them removed

explanation.surface: A sports team with its best players gone, narrowly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipped' suggests beaten by a whisker; it means stoned, as fruit is.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit whose pips have been taken out, or bred without them, contains no kernels.

clue.text: One is wrong about French word for 'feelings'

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the French piece
set wrong, the letters are reordered

parts.note: mot is French for word

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken about the French term for feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' looks like the verb of the sentence, but 'is' joins 'One' as the letters that 'wrong' rearranges into EIONS, which then wraps MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy, anger and fear are all sentiments: plural synonym.

clue.text: Face beaten up, cut by a right, showing bottle

indicators.note: the mangled face is cut into by the letters that follow
a battered face is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A battered face, slashed by a right-hander, shows the bottle used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' rearranges FACE into CAFE, which 'cut by' then opens after its C for A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass jug or decanter for wine or water at table is a kind of bottle.

clue.text: We're paying for it and it's a burden

definitions.meaning: a treat or round '...' is paid for by the speakers
a duty or responsibility placed on someone

explanation.surface: Footing the bill together turns out to be heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for load is used in English for a responsibility or obligation.

clue.text: Softens, going to pieces, doesn't confess

indicators.note: falling apart, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: to own up is to confess; own alone carries that sense

explanation.surface: A suspect cracks under pressure yet still won't admit anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pieces' rearranges DOESNT plus OWN, with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate or make something less harsh, like a colour or statement, is to soften it.

clue.text: All alone, missing one after drink

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the drink

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: the letters of the word one are taken out

explanation.surface: Drinking by oneself after a dram, everything else gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing one' removes O, N and E from ALONE, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole amount, the sum of everything, is the complete figure: same sense.

clue.text: Double string and cut off end

indicators.note: the last letter of the string word is removed

parts.note: twine is strong string

explanation.surface: Doubling up some string and snipping off the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off end' removes E from TWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact look-alike or matching counterpart is someone's double.

clue.text: Plumbing installed to no purpose?

parts.note: a pointless fitting is a waste; the joke reads a drain outlet as a pipe fitted in vain

explanation.surface: A plumber fits pipes that serve no function.
explanation.walkthrough: To waste is to squander, but the outlet carries away waste water, so it has a very real purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The drain carrying used water away from a sink or bath is the plumbing outlet.

clue.text: Witnesses witnessed entering with planks

indicators.note: the past-tense word goes into the present-tense word

parts.note: one who witnesses something sees it
the past tense of see

explanation.surface: Witnesses come into court with lengths of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link here, not an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground teeter-totter is a long board pivoted at the middle, so each is a plank.

clue.text: Got reminder about antidote

indicators.note: the nudge word goes around the remedy word

parts.note: a prod is a nudge to remember
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Someone received a reminder about a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or acquire something, often with effort, is to get it.

clue.text: Sends up a lot too high

definitions.text: Sends up a lot too high

parts.words: Sends up a lot too high
parts.note: at auction a lot is an item for sale; pushing its price up too far is offering too much

explanation.surface: Seems to describe launching something far too high, like a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sends up' sounds like mockery or a launch, and 'a lot' like 'much'; at auction a lot is the item and sending it up is raising the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering more than an item is worth at a sale pushes the price up for that lot.

clue.text: Prepares for test in French, dreams one's got through

indicators.note: the possessive piece passes inside the French word

parts.note: the French for dreams is rêves
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A student cramming for a French exam dreams of passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got through' suggests passing the exam; here IS goes through REVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over notes before an exam is the British sense of studying for it.

clue.text: Steal underwear

definitions.meaning: to ... away is to steal off quietly
a petticoat or light undergarment worn under a dress

explanation.surface: Pinching lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' looks like theft; it is the sense of moving off stealthily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a quiet departure and a woman's undergarment share the word.

clue.text: Unwilling to take laziness, head dismissed

indicators.note: the first letter of the idleness word is removed

parts.note: sloth is idleness

explanation.surface: A boss reluctant to tolerate idleness sacks the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head dismissed' removes S from SLOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant, not wanting to do something, is a mostly literary variant of loath.

clue.text: Advocate of traditional practices did ornate old instrument cases

indicators.note: the instrument encloses the other letters as in a case

parts.note: the lute is an early plucked string instrument

indicators.note: made fancy, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A traditionalist decorated old instrument cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' rearranges DID into DDI, which LUTE 'cases'.
explanation.definitionFit: The followers of Ned Ludd smashed machines; the name now means someone opposed to new technology.

clue.text: Riddle of motorway being obliterated in mist and downpour

indicators.note: wiped out, so these letters disappear from the weather words

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI
heavy rain

explanation.surface: The mystery of a motorway vanishing in mist and rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle; it is a sieve. MI is the M1, the London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve, and to sieve liquid or soil through mesh is to sift it.

clue.text: Likewise, no member of the hoi polloi

definitions.text: no member of the hoi polloi
definitions.meaning: ... is a smart, fashionable person, the opposite of the common masses

explanation.surface: Similarly, someone who isn't one of the common people.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into A plus SWELL, an old word for a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means also or too, matching likewise.

clue.text: Vulgarity often rejected by editor, to be replaced by literary stars?

definitions.text: Vulgarity often rejected by editor, to be replaced by literary stars?

parts.words: Vulgarity often rejected by editor, to be replaced by literary stars?
parts.note: a swear word in print is often cut by an editor and shown as asterisks, the literary stars

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an editor swapping crude prose for famous authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literary stars' suggests celebrated writers; it means asterisks (Greek for little stars) printed in place of a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude swear word or oath is a vulgarity that editors replace with asterisks.

clue.text: Shows animal inside, frolicking about

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the animal word
playing about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal kept indoors, romping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like a position for the animal, but it is the fodder 'frolicking' rearranges, which then goes 'about' CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out or signal something is to show it.

clue.text: Blows caught mouth?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the lips stand for the mouth

explanation.surface: Punches landing on someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Light smacks or cuffs, such as a clip round the ear, are blows.

clue.text: No good cultivating fruit

indicators.note: this word says the good letter is absent

parts.note: raising crops is cultivating them

explanation.surface: Growing crops is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' reads as useless; 'No' removes G from RAISING.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Alleviate unsteady gait in time, undergoing treatment

indicators.note: the shaky walk goes inside the treated time
being treated, these letters are worked into a new form
not steady, so the letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Easing a patient's shaky walk with treatment over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteady' turns GAIT into TIGA, which goes 'in' MITE, from TIME 'undergoing treatment'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen pain or severity is to ease or relieve it.

clue.text: More than one beautiful person breaks down, keeping quiet

indicators.note: the failure word holds the call for silence

parts.note: an engine that breaks down dies
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone collapses but keeps the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' suggests weeping; it is a machine failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is informal for a good-looking person, so the plural is several of them.

clue.text: Main salon's modified according to time of year

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea

indicators.note: changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand hairdressing salon redecorated for the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective; it is the sea. 's is 'has' as a link; 'modified' turns SALON into SONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something varying with or typical of a particular part of the year is timed by it.
